Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
254 PM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Cold temperatures and areas of freezing fog this morning,
  followed by mostly dry weather today through Tuesday afternoon.

* A weak storm brings increased winds and light Sierra snow 
  Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. 

* Dry and mild weather is favored for Thanksgiving Day into the
  weekend with additional storms possible late next weekend and 
  beyond. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

For Tuesday, a ridge will quickly move through the region. This 
will increase high temperatures around 2-4 degrees compared to 
Monday. We are looking at mid-40s to low-50s for the western 
Nevada valleys, and upper-30s to mid-40s for northeast CA, and for
eastern Sierra communities. 

Our next system is moving into the area late Tuesday. This will 
introduce a 10-20% chance for light precipitation in western 
Lassen County by the late evening. For Wednesday, a weak system 
will quickly transit through the area. This system is looking less
impressive with each model run. Latest Hi-Res model guidance from
the REFS and NBM shows light precipitation accumulations, 
generally 0.10 inches or less in the eastern Sierra north of Lake
Tahoe. Very little to no precipitation is forecasted for the 
remainder of the eastern Sierra south of Lake Tahoe as well as 
western NV. The best chance for measurable precipitation will 
occur around Lassen National Park where amounts are between 
0.10-0.15 inches. Snow amounts look unimpressive, with around a 
trace to 1 inch snow above 6,500 feet toward Lassen Park. 

By late Wednesday into the weekend, a ridge of high pressure 
builds over the western US. This will allow for temperatures to 
increase back to seasonal averages by Thanksgiving, then above 
average into the weekend. Under high pressure, we'll maintain 
calm, dry weather. However, with high pressure, stronger 
inversions will form each day into the weekend. By Sunday into the
start of next week, model ensembles are showing an active pattern
setting up over the region. But, there is a lot of uncertainty 
in rain, higher elevation snow, and winds. -McKellar

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions and light breezes prevail today into 
Tuesday. Mid to high level clouds begin to increase this afternoon 
ahead of an approaching weak storm. 

Regional Outlook: Low chance (less than 20%) of FZFG will lead to
periods of LIFR conditions at KTRK through 16-17Z this morning. 
Otherwise, VFR conditions and light breezes prevail through 
Tuesday morning.


24-72 Hour Outlook: A weak Pacific storm will increase winds and 
bring light snow showers to Tahoe terminals Tuesday night and 
Wednesday morning. A 15% chance of -SN at KTRK-KTVL may reduce 
CIGS/VIS to MVFR conditions Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. 
SW FL100 flow increases to around 35 kts Tuesday afternoon from 
Tahoe northward, posing LLWS and mountain wave turbulence impacts 
at KTRK- KTVL and KRNO-KCXP-KMEV into Tuesday night. 

-Salas/McKellar
